$comment: Machine-readable delta registry for hermes-agent. Every change we carry on top of the pinned upstream tag lives here with the reason and the condition under which it can be dropped; hermes-upstream-check.mjs compares it against upstream and flags the deltas upstream has caught up with. Docs: docs/myrmidon/hermes-deltas.md. Keep pinnedRef/pinnedVersion in sync with docker/bot-runtime/Dockerfile (the checker fails when they disagree). `source` stays the upstream repository (that is what the pin is compared against); the image itself clones `docker/bot-runtime/Dockerfile`'s HERMES_REPO, our mirror fork — see the 'Not deltas' section of the docs.

hindsightPlugin.$comment: The memory provider we vendor, recorded here (not read from a file: the hermes catalog entry lives inside the hermes checkout, not in this repository). The image reads plugin-catalog/hindsight.yaml from the pinned hermes tag and fails the build when this pin disagrees; the checker probes the plugin's own default branch.

deltas.reason: The bash session snapshot lives in a shared temp dir and every profile in a container runs as one uid, so credential-shaped env values dumped there were readable by a neighbouring profile.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream excludes credential-shaped env names from the session snapshot by itself.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: publishing to a third-party repository needs the publisher-scan wrapper (plan item PUBLISH-SCAN), which does not exist; the text is prepared in the ticket for the operator to submit.

deltas.reason: The stock asyncio default executor is small and a live run holds one worker for its whole life, so the board's POST /v1/runs create calls timed out behind parallel runs.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream sizes the gateway's default executor above the fleet's concurrent runs, or ships an equivalent setting.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: Before every state-DB write the gateway probes whether the WAL/SHM generation this handle opened is still on disk. When the handle has no recorded sidecar identity the probe readlinks every open descriptor of the process on the calling thread — the gateway's event loop. A state.db reached through a symlink never records an identity (SQLite puts -wal/-shm next to the link target, so the literal <path>-wal never stats), so a multi-profile gateway with hundreds of descriptors walked /proc/self/fd once per write and starved the out-of-loop liveness watchdog into a hard exit (75), failing every run in flight. Same verdict, at most one walk per second per handle.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream stops walking /proc/self/fd on the write path: a cached probe verdict, a minimum interval between probes, or the probe moved off the caller's thread.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: The run harness removes each run's scratch dir at the run boundary. A path remembered mid-session then succeeds again the moment a write tool's folded mkdir -p re-creates the missing paperclip-run-* parent: mode 755, no run-scratch marker file, never reclaimed — unmarked residue in the shared /tmp holding payloads and comment bodies readable to every co-tenant agent in the container. The guard refuses a write whose ancestor is a removed run-scratch root; a live root and dirs outside the class are untouched, and the guard fails open on its own errors.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships an equivalent guard in agent/file_safety.py / tools/file_operations.py: a write into a removed run-scratch root is refused instead of re-creating it.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: Same change as delta 07: the guard has to run on both write paths the model can reach (write_file, patch_replace) and at the _atomic_write chokepoint where the folded mkdir -p lives, which also covers the V4A patch path. The two patches are one change, split only to keep the diffs file-sized.
deltas.dropCondition: Same as delta 07: upstream refuses a write into a removed run-scratch root on its own write paths.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: The board mints a run-bound github_credentials capability for container agents, but a hermes gateway has no per-run process to inherit env from, so the capability had no delivery path and container agents could not push. /v1/runs now accepts a github_broker body field and binds it per-run through contextvars; the terminal child-env bridge exports it to that run's subprocesses only.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships a per-run credential-delivery field on /v1/runs with equivalent concurrency isolation.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: The catalog Hindsight plugin uses one shared client timeout for recall, retain and reflect, and has no way to skip the expensive consolidated-observations layer; a reflect call routinely outlives a recall-sized timeout. The in-tree provider we used to patch had a reflect-specific timeout, a fact-type filter and a bounded retry on the bank's 503 admission refusal.
deltas.dropCondition: The catalog plugin gains a reflect-specific timeout (or a per-operation timeout), a reflect fact-type filter, or the 503 retry.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: the change is small and self-contained but publishing to a third-party repository needs the publisher-scan wrapper (plan item PUBLISH-SCAN) first; the offer text is prepared in the ticket for the operator.

deltas.reason: The board issues task workspaces via myr-ws, but the hermes gateway had no delivery path: /v1/runs now accepts a workspace body field, opens the task copy with myr-ws open before the model starts, binds it as the run cwd and exports MYRMIDON_TASK_WORKSPACE to that run's subprocesses; myr-ws exit codes 3/4/5 fall back to /scratch with a warning run event instead of a silent failure (BOT-DISK-H5b).
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships a workspace-open hook on /v1/runs with equivalent cwd/env delivery and failure signaling.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: Part A stages the managed Git launcher (the git/gh wrappers plus git-credential-paperclip) on a local or SSH execution target, but an agent that starts through the hermes_gateway adapter has no execution target on the board side, so the staged directory never existed where its runs happen and it kept pushing with a static token. /v1/runs now accepts a github_launcher body field, stages the bodies in the gateway's own temp root under the run id, and binds PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_LAUNCHER_DIR/PATH/ZDOTDIR/BASH_ENV/GH_CONFIG_DIR for that run's children only; the credential the staged programs resolve still comes from the run's github_broker capability.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships a per-run launcher/credential-helper delivery field on /v1/runs with equivalent concurrency isolation.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: A live board key (pcp_ + family + opaque body) reached the delegation live transcript verbatim: every existing matcher in agent/redact.py needs a KEY=, header or JSON-field shape, and transcript prose (subagent result text, CLI echo, error message) carries none of them. Six bare-token prefix patterns — pcp_, pcp_board_, pcp_cli_auth_, pcp_invite_, pcp_bootstrap_, pcp_claim_ — join _PREFIX_PATTERNS so the generic pass masks the key wherever it appears. Bodies are controlled per family: invite tokens are base64url(32 bytes), so the invite pattern takes [A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,} (an alphanumeric-only body silently fails to match whenever a separator lands in the first 20 chars, because the compiled matcher's trailing lookahead forbids ending the run before a '-'/'_'); the other five keep [A-Za-z0-9]{20,} so the short form cannot swallow legitimate pcp_board_-style config slugs. One pattern per family: the engine validator rejects top-level alternation, and one merged grouped alternative would force a single body class on all families; a grouped pcp_(?:board|cli_auth|...)_ prefix would also drop the extracted literal prefix to 'pcp_' only — per-family patterns keep full literal prefixes for the pre-screen.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships a bare-token prefix family covering the pcp_ key prefixes in agent/redact.py.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending). The pattern family is board-specific anyway; the general defect upstream owns is that no bare-token pass exists for vendor prefixes outside its list.

deltas.reason: LiveTranscriptWriter created task-N.log with path.write_text(), i.e. 0o644 & ~umask — world-readable under the image's umask 022. The transcripts live in a shared bot container under HERMES_HOME/delegation/live/ and survive 7 days, so any co-tenant process could read them; combined with the missing pcp_ redaction (delta 12) a live board key was readable container-wide. The header write now goes through tempfile.mkstemp(dir=...) + os.replace, which creates the file 0o600 without a mode argument, so there is no chmod race and no world-readable window; later event() appends touch an existing 0o600 file.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream creates delegation live transcripts owner-only (0o600).
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending). This one is a generic security fix worth offering on its own once the publish path exists.

deltas.reason: The hermes_gateway adapter has no filesystem access to the gateway and the API surface has no profile-skills write endpoint, so Paperclip-managed skills could not reach gateway agents at all. /v1/runs now accepts a paperclip_skills body field ([{path, name, content}]); _run_agent_sync materializes the entries into the run profile's skills/paperclip-managed/ segment (inside _profile_scope, before the model starts), verifies every desired entry landed and fails the run with 'Cannot start without the required Paperclip-managed skills' otherwise, and binds MYRMIDON_RUN_SKILLS_DIR for that run's child processes only. Removal touches only the profile's own managed segment (1.6.6-HERMES-SKILLS-A).
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships a per-run skill-delivery field on /v1/runs with equivalent profile-scoped materialization and verification.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: A turn persists its user row before the first model call, so a failed run leaves its prompt as the unanswered tail of the session. The board re-dispatches a fresh, not byte-identical prompt for the same session and every retry added another user row; the live-replay merge then sent them all as one user message (43 rows of about 220 KB became a single 9.6 MB message) that the provider rejected again and again. A /v1/runs run now supersedes the stranded tail prompts that share its prompt's head (soft-delete through SessionDB.rewind_user_turn, dropped from the history in place).
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream replaces or adopts an unanswered tail prompt on /v1/runs retries whose text is not identical.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: Every model call re-sends the whole session; quotas are consumed by fresh (uncached) input and a provider cache hits only on a byte-identical prefix, so rewriting a message that was already sent turns the rest of the context into fresh input. The patch carries the logic and the settings (config.yaml `context_economy:` block) of the token economy: measure A (every wake message but the newest becomes a one-line note) and measure B (stale heavy tool results become notes with a ref; the new read_stale_tool_result tool returns the original) rewrite earlier rows of the request copy, so both are off by default and kept behind config keys; the wake detection recognises the adapter's current and pre-rename identity heads (it had gone dead at the rename) and skill_view and reads of skill files are never replaced. At a compaction, which breaks the cache anyway, wake packages are not quoted into the summarizer input and the summary's verbatim user messages. HERMES_KEEP_STALE_WAKES=1 and HERMES_KEEP_STALE_TOOL_RESULTS=1 force A and B off.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream trims superseded task prompts and stale tool results of the replayed history on the send path, with a way to read the original back.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: agent.disabled_toolsets works on whole toolsets, but the browser credential vault rides with the browser and vision_analyze has a toolset of its own next to tools the role uses, so their schemas (about 1.2k tokens) were sent on every call by roles that never call them. model_tools._select_tool_names now also subtracts the tools listed under agent.disabled_tools in config.yaml.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream offers a per-tool disable list next to agent.disabled_toolsets.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: worker-owned async writer acquire: one awaited scan, connect and registry/cache ownership transaction. Includes full OPE-7854 lifecycle A-G implementation.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream implements the complete OPE-7854 A-G contract: strict complete scanner verdict before every writer connect, one shared sync/async registry, cancellation-safe ownership and cache drain, async lazy profile/routing/recovery opens, and awaited gateway startup/shutdown lifecycle.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: publisher-scan wrapper is not available.

deltas.reason: Upstream _AUTH_HEADER_RE in agent/redact.py unconditionally masked any token following Authorization: Bearer, swallowing enclosing backticks and leading Bearer into *** when inspecting code template strings (e.g. `authorization: `Bearer ${token}``). This resulted in syntax corruption (`authorization: *** ${token}`) in tool outputs, leading to false-positive review rejections. The patch preserves enclosing quotes and backticks in _AUTH_HEADER_RE and introduces _is_probable_auth_secret to distinguish genuine high-entropy credentials (Bearer ghp_... 36+ chars, JWTs, opaque tokens) from code template syntax (${...}, <...>, {...}) and variable names ($token, authToken).
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream distinguishes code template syntax and variable identifiers from genuine credentials in authorization header redaction and preserves enclosing quote delimiters.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.

deltas.reason: A bot gateway container is long-lived and serves many runs, so the container-level PAPERCLIP_RUN_ID/MYRMIDON_RUN_ID in os.environ belongs to whichever run happened to start the container and is stale for every later run. An agent reading $PAPERCLIP_RUN_ID and sending it as X-Paperclip-Run-Id on a board mutation got a stale value and the board answered 409 Issue run ownership conflict, blocking decision writes (OPE-10358). _run_agent_sync now binds the board run id through contextvars for the whole turn; the terminal child-env bridge in local.py overrides the inherited (stale) container-level value for that run's subprocesses only. OPE-10602: the rc.29 image bound the gateway's INTERNAL run id (run_<hex>) — not a board UUID — and every agent board mutation 500ed with invalid input syntax for type uuid: "run_...", so reviewers could not write verdicts. The board adapter now always sends the board run id as the X-Paperclip-Run-Id request header; _handle_runs validates it to a UUID (400 on malformed), _run_agent_sync binds ONLY that value — never run.run_id — and set_run_id_vars refuses to bind anything that is not a UUID. Without the header (older boards) nothing is bound.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships a per-run run-id binding for gateway-spawned children fed from an explicit, caller-supplied board run id, or the board stops enforcing run ownership on agent mutations.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: Propagates configured max_tokens / max_output_tokens from config.yaml into agent and custom OpenAI-compatible provider request kwargs; resets length_continue_retries to 0 after a successful tool round; and escalates ephemeral max output tokens on truncation retry without relying solely on reasoning_effort=none for persistent thinking models.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream Hermes reads configured max_tokens for custom providers, resets length retry counters after tool steps, and scales output budget on truncation retries.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.

deltas.reason: Upstream persists a tool result only above 100000 characters (50000 for mcp_ tools) and then shows a 1500-character preview, so a 20 KB command output rides every later request in full. A new result longer than context_economy.tool_result_max_chars (16000) is now stored and sent as its first 8000 and last 4000 characters plus a marker that names the spill file holding the whole text and how to read the middle. The result is shaped once, before any provider has seen it, so the provider cache is untouched. read_file stays pinned by upstream, skill_view is exempt, 0 gives the upstream limits back.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream bounds an oversized tool result by head and tail with a configurable threshold and a way to read the rest.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.

deltas.reason: A compaction rewrites the messages, but the tool schemas and the system prompt in front of them can stay byte-identical and keep their provider cache. The upstream rebuild at the compaction boundary invalidates the cached prompt, re-reads memory, re-renders plugin sections, re-lists skills and re-lists MCP tools, which changes those bytes whenever any of it moved during the session. With context_economy.compaction_keep_prefix (default on) the cached prompt and the tool array are kept.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream keeps the system prompt and the tool array byte-stable at a compaction unless something requires a rebuild.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.

deltas.reason: Upstream's providers.<id>.session_affinity_header puts the conversation key in a request header. The pool of ChatGPT accounts behind the LiteLLM gateway also routes its prompt cache on the request body's prompt_cache_key, which the chat-completions transport sends only to api.openai.com and to provider profiles that declare support, never to a custom endpoint, so the body key was absent. An endpoint whose providers entry names the option now gets the same key (the header's own value) in the body, bounded to 64 characters like every key; a key the caller pinned stays, and every endpoint without the option is untouched.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream sends the conversation key as prompt_cache_key for an endpoint that opted in with session_affinity_header.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.

deltas.reason: Every model of a bot is reached through one gateway, so a lost connection to it fails the primary and every fallback alike. Upstream treated a connect failure as any transport error: one more attempt, the fallback chain after the second failure, and the run stayed on the fallback until its end (the primary is restored only at the start of the next turn), so a gateway restart of about a minute moved a run onto a paid model. An error that says the gateway is not answering (no HTTP answer: connection refused or reset, connect timeout, APIConnectionError; or a 502/503/504 whose text names no model and no provider) is now retried against the primary with the growing pause for up to HERMES_GATEWAY_OUTAGE_BUDGET_S seconds (180) before any fallback; errors of a model or a provider (429, quota, model not found, no healthy deployments, overload, read timeout) go to the fallback as before. A run on a fallback tries the primary again every HERMES_FALLBACK_PROBE_EVERY model calls (10) and stays on it when the call succeeds.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream tells an unreachable endpoint from a model or provider error before it walks the fallback chain, and lets a run on a fallback return to the primary inside the turn.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.

deltas.reason: Upstream runs the automatic VACUUM of state.db only in a pass whose own prune deleted a session. The bot runtime deletes old sessions through the API when a container starts, before hermes' first maintenance tick, so the tick's prune found nothing and none of the 65 databases was ever vacuumed (15.6 GB of 39.9 GB were free pages). The VACUUM now runs on the freelist share alone (above 25%, at most once per min_vacuum_interval_days), after checking that no turn is running (session turn leases in the store, the gateway's running turns), that the database's volume has twice the live data free and that SQLite's temp directory is not RAM; otherwise it waits and the pass is retried by the next housekeeping tick. The bot entrypoint sets SQLITE_TMPDIR to the data volume so the temporary copy of the live data is not charged to the container's memory.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream vacuums on the freelist share alone and checks the free space and the temp directory before the rewrite.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.

deltas.reason: Unifies context compaction summary structure across fresh, iterative-update, and deterministic fallback summaries into 9 standardized sections: USER_CONTEXT, TASK_TRACKING, COMPLETED, PENDING, CURRENT_STATE, CODE_STATE, TESTS, CHANGES, VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS, with verbatim task/ticket IDs and PR numbers, while preserving legacy task snapshot heading parsers.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream adopts a 9-section structured compaction summary with verbatim task and ticket ID tracking.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet.
